brief: NVDA lost $2.7tr in market cap over six weeks. Goldman's Pasquariello says most of the S&P's drop from the October 6 highs through November 11 traces to that one stock, turning a single-name bear market into a market-wide one. The AI narrative flipped (slowing capex growth, shifting politics, a surge in cyberattacks), so the bank's AI-leaders basket is now down on the year after being up 53% YTD five months ago. Pasquariello reads this as the market re-pricing AI as a cycle with a peak, not a permanent theme. The selloff was worsened by thin liquidity (SPX top-of-book depth near its YTD low) as funds sold and dealers ran short gamma and vol, and by a Fed still hiking, which Pasquariello says removes the Fed put. For a bottom, Goldman's Lee cites hedge fund deleveraging (GS Prime net leverage at the 1st percentile) as a good sign, but says broader positioning (mutual fund and ETF inflows, the GS Sentiment Indicator at the 75th percentile) has not washed out, and that panic readings above 9 during Fed hikes have historically preceded flat three-month returns. Pasquariello still calls the vol high in. ZeroHedge calls him early on everything else.
